signals.name: More reliable community and content research for coding agents
signals.hypothesis: Coding-agent users need a community and content research workflow that reduces generic or assumption-heavy results and binds decisions to traceable evidence.
signals.decision_relevance: A portable Agent Skill can fill the gap without requiring a hosted scraper or proprietary research harness.
alternative_explanations: The observed need may be satisfied by better prompts or bespoke multi-agent workflows rather than a reusable skill.
A purposive Reddit sample can overrepresent users motivated to complain or optimize their workflows.
signals.disconfirming_evidence_needed: Cold comparisons showing that a simpler prompt or existing public skill produces equally traceable decisions with fewer errors and less effort.

signals.name: Skills that encode a testable procedure
signals.hypothesis: Skill users value repeatable procedures, schemas, and objective tests more than generic expertise personas or reminders.
signals.decision_relevance: The research skill should include concrete data contracts and an executable audit rather than prose alone.
alternative_explanations: The discussion comes from one thread and may reflect a local norm rather than a recurring cross-thread need.
Users may prefer short reminder-style skills when the task is simple.
signals.disconfirming_evidence_needed: Independent threads or controlled comparisons showing generic persona skills are equally consistent and testable.
